objects.description: State machine step indicator for base64 encoding. Values progress through steps A, B, and C while processing input bytes into base64 output.

Holds the mutable state for streaming base64 encoding, including the current step and any carry-over bits in result. Must be initialized before use with base64_init_encodestate and then passed to block encode functions.
State machine step indicator for base64 decoding. Values progress through steps a–d while converting base64 input characters into bytes.

Holds the mutable state for streaming base64 decoding, including current step and any pending output byte in plainchar. Must be initialized before use with base64_init_decodestate and then passed to block decode functions.

functions.name: base64_init_encodestate
functions.description: Initializes a base64_encodestate for subsequent streaming base64 encoding. Call this before the first call to base64_encode_block (or when restarting a new encoding sequence). The function resets the internal step and result fields so encoding starts at a block boundary.
requirements: state_in must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct base64_encodestate allocated by the caller.
Must be called before using the state with base64_encode_block/base64_encode_blockend for a new encoding sequence.
Do not use the same state_in concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: base64_encode_value
functions.description: Encodes a 6-bit value into its Base64 alphabet character. Typically used internally by higher-level encoding routines but can be used directly if manually composing Base64 output. Exact mapping and behavior for out-of-range input are not documented here.
requirements: value_in is expected to represent a 6-bit value in the range [0, 63]; behavior for values outside this range is unspecified (inferred from name and common Base64 practice).

functions.name: base64_encode_block
functions.signature: int base64_encode_block(const char *plaintext_in, int length_in, char *code_out, struct base64_encodestate *state_in);
functions.description: Encodes a block of binary data into Base64 text using a streaming state. May be called repeatedly to process large inputs in chunks; maintains state across calls via state_in. Returns the number of characters written to code_out for this call. Call base64_encode_blockend after the final block to flush any remaining output and padding.
requirements: plaintext_in must point to at least length_in bytes of readable memory.
length_in must be >= 0.
code_out must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the Base64 output produced for this block; the exact maximum expansion ratio is at least ceil(length_in/3)*4 (inferred from Base64).
state_in must be non-null and initialized via base64_init_encodestate before the first block in a sequence; reuse the same state_in across subsequent blocks of the same sequence.
The return value is the number of bytes written to code_out; the caller should use it to advance output pointers and must not assume null-termination.
Do not call concurrently on the same state_in without external synchronization.

functions.name: base64_encode_blockend
functions.description: Finalizes a streaming Base64 encoding sequence by emitting any remaining encoded characters and padding. Returns the number of characters appended to code_out. Invoke after the last call to base64_encode_block for a sequence.
requirements: code_out must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold any remaining output and padding; exact maximum is not specified here (commonly up to 4 characters; inferred).
state_in must be non-null and must refer to the same encoding state used for the sequence, previously initialized by base64_init_encodestate.
Should be called exactly once at the end of each encoding sequence before reusing or reinitializing the state.
The return value is the number of bytes written; output is not null-terminated unless done by the caller.

functions.name: base64_init_decodestate
functions.description: Initializes a base64_decodestate for streaming Base64 decoding. Call before the first call to base64_decode_block (or when starting a new decoding sequence). Resets internal step and accumulator.
requirements: state_in must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct base64_decodestate allocated by the caller.
Must be called before using the state with base64_decode_block for a new decoding sequence.
Do not use the same state_in concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: base64_decode_value
functions.description: Converts a Base64 character to its 6-bit decoded value. Typically used internally by the decoder. Behavior for characters outside the Base64 alphabet (including padding '=') is not specified here.
requirements: value_in is expected to be a Base64 alphabet character (ASCII) or related input; exact handling of non-alphabet characters is unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: base64_decode_block
functions.signature: int base64_decode_block(const char *code_in, int length_in, char *plaintext_out, struct base64_decodestate *state_in);
functions.description: Decodes a block of Base64-encoded text into binary data using a streaming state. May be called repeatedly on successive chunks; maintains state across calls. Returns the number of bytes written to plaintext_out for this call.
requirements: code_in must point to at least length_in bytes of readable memory containing Base64 text; the function may accept padding '=' and possibly ignore non-alphabet characters (behavior not fully specified here; inferred).
length_in must be >= 0.
plaintext_out must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the decoded output; worst-case decoded length is at most (length_in/4)*3 for well-formed input (inferred from Base64).
state_in must be non-null and initialized via base64_init_decodestate before the first block in a sequence; reuse the same state_in across subsequent blocks of the same sequence.
The return value is the number of bytes written to plaintext_out; output is not null-terminated unless done by the caller.
Do not call concurrently on the same state_in without external synchronization.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for base64_decode_block.
# The fuzzer uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR to obtain a string of bytes (not necessarily ASCII).
# We will generate valid and interesting Base64 text chunks, including variations:
# - Properly padded 4-char blocks
# - No padding for lengths %3 != 0 across chunk boundaries
# - Inclusion of whitespace and line breaks
# - URL-safe vs standard alphabet switches (still often accepted by tolerant decoders)
# - Mixed case, empty input, single/partial quanta to trigger state machine transitions
# - Random chunk sizes up to 1024 bytes (fuzzer caps to 1024)
# The output must be valid bytes and <= 4096 bytes.

_B64_STD = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
_B64_URL = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_"

_WHITESPACE_BYTES = [b" ", b"\t", b"\r", b"\n"]


def _rand(r: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return r.randint(lo, hi)


def _choose(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]


def _random_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _b64_encode_block(data: bytes, alphabet: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Encode arbitrary bytes to base64 using provided alphabet (no newlines, with padding as needed)
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    L = len(data)
    while i + 3 <= L:
        b0, b1, b2 = data[i], data[i+1], data[i+2]
        i += 3
        out.append(alphabet[b0 >> 2])
        out.append(alphabet[((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)])
        out.append(alphabet[((b1 & 0x0F) << 2) | (b2 >> 6)])
        out.append(alphabet[b2 & 0x3F])
    rem = L - i
    if rem == 1:
        b0 = data[i]
        out.append(alphabet[b0 >> 2])
        out.append(alphabet[(b0 & 0x03) << 4])
        out.append(ord(b'='))
        out.append(ord(b'='))
    elif rem == 2:
        b0, b1 = data[i], data[i+1]
        out.append(alphabet[b0 >> 2])
        out.append(alphabet[((b0 & 0x03) << 4) | (b1 >> 4)])
        out.append(alphabet[(b1 & 0x0F) << 2])
        out.append(ord(b'='))
    return bytes(out)


def _maybe_strip_padding(r: random.Random, b64: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Some decoders allow missing padding; produce variants without '=' at end
    if not b64:
        return b64
    # Only strip if padding exists and with some probability
    if b64.endswith(b'=') and r.random() < 0.4:
        # strip one or two '='
        if b64.endswith(b'==') and r.random() < 0.5:
            return b64[:-2]
        return b64[:-1]
    return b64


def _inject_whitespace(r: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not data:
        return data
    # Insert whitespace at random positions; keep total size reasonable
    out = bytearray()
    for i, ch in enumerate(data):
        out.append(ch)
        if r.random() < 0.05:
            ws = _choose(r, _WHITESPACE_BYTES)
            out.extend(ws)
    # Maybe add leading/trailing whitespace
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        out = bytearray(_choose(r, _WHITESPACE_BYTES)) + out
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        out.extend(_choose(r, _WHITESPACE_BYTES))
    return bytes(out)


def _mix_alphabets(r: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Swap '+'<->'-' and '/'<->'_' randomly to test URL-safe tolerance
    if not data or r.random() < 0.5:
        return data
    trans = bytearray(range(256))
    trans[ord('+')] = ord('-')
    trans[ord('/')] = ord('_')
    trans[ord('-')] = ord('+')
    trans[ord('_')] = ord('/')
    return data.translate(bytes(trans))


def _chunked_stream_sequence(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a sequence simulating streaming boundaries: concat partial quanta pieces
    # We create several chunks encoded independently and then optionally strip padding
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    num_chunks = _rand(r, 1, 8)
    for _ in range(num_chunks):
        # size biased to create various remainders
        size_choice = r.random()
        if size_choice < 0.2:
            n = 0
        elif size_choice < 0.5:
            n = _rand(r, 1, 2)
        else:
            n = _rand(r, 3, 48)
        alphabet = _B64_STD if r.random() < 0.7 else _B64_URL
        raw = _random_bytes(r, n)
        enc = _b64_encode_block(raw, alphabet)
        enc = _maybe_strip_padding(r, enc)
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            enc = _inject_whitespace(r, enc)
        parts.append(enc)
        # Occasionally insert explicit newlines between chunks
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(_choose(r, _WHITESPACE_BYTES))
    data = b"".join(parts)
    # Mix alphabets post-concatenation sometimes
    data = _mix_alphabets(r, data)
    # Ensure cap to 1024 as fuzzer will cap; we keep smaller
    if len(data) > 1024:
        data = data[:1024]
    return data


def _pure_valid_block(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate a single, clean Base64 string for well-formed decoding
    n = _rand(r, 0, 256)
    raw = _random_bytes(r, n)
    alphabet = _B64_STD if r.random() < 0.7 else _B64_URL
    enc = _b64_encode_block(raw, alphabet)
    # Maybe wrap at 76 columns like MIME
    if r.random() < 0.4 and len(enc) > 0:
        width = _choose(r, [64, 76])
        wrapped = bytearray()
        for i in range(0, len(enc), width):
            wrapped.extend(enc[i:i+width])
            wrapped.append(ord('\n'))
        enc = bytes(wrapped)
    # Maybe remove padding to test tolerance
    enc = _maybe_strip_padding(r, enc)
    return enc[:1024]


def _edge_cases(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    return [
        b"",  # empty
        b"=",  # lone padding
        b"==",  # double padding
        b"A===",  # excessive padding
        b"AAAA",  # decodes to 3 zero bytes
        b"AAA=",  # invalid padding position, but interesting
        b"TWFu",  # "Man"
        b"TWE=",  # "Ma"
        b"TQ==",  # "M"
        b"YW55IGNhcm5hbCBwbGVhc3VyZS4=",  # classic lorem fragment
        b"YW55IGNhcm5hbCBwbGVhc3VyZS4\n\n",  # with blank lines
        b"aW5wdXQvdXJsLXNhZmU_",  # URL-safe variant with '?'
        b"LS0tLy8vKysrX19f",  # mix of URL-safe and std chars in text
    ]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        data = _pure_valid_block(r)
    elif choice < 0.6:
        data = _chunked_stream_sequence(r)
    elif choice < 0.85:
        data = _choose(r, _edge_cases(r))
    else:
        # Construct sequence intended to exercise decoder state transitions across boundaries
        # Alternate short fragments that leave the state mid-quantum
        fragments: List[bytes] = []
        # Start with a valid base64 for 1 or 2 leftover bytes, then strip padding
        n = _choose(r, [1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 10])
        raw = _random_bytes(r, n)
        enc = _b64_encode_block(raw, _B64_STD)
        enc = _maybe_strip_padding(r, enc)
        fragments.append(enc)
        # Insert whitespace and some random valid alphabet characters
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            fragments.append(_inject_whitespace(r, b""))
        # Add a few random valid characters to finish a quantum
        alphabet = _B64_STD
        for _ in range(_rand(r, 1, 6)):
            fragments.append(bytes([_choose(r, alphabet)]))
        # Possibly add a properly padded ending
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            tail_raw = _random_bytes(r, _rand(r, 0, 6))
            tail = _b64_encode_block(tail_raw, _B64_STD)
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                tail = _maybe_strip_padding(r, tail)
            fragments.append(_inject_whitespace(r, tail))
        data = b"".join(fragments)[:1024]

    # Ensure bytes and size limit per requirements
    if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
        data = bytes(data)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return bytes(data)
